O1.citation: “One passing run is a single observation, not proof that the skill reliably works” and “the defensible claim is only: ‘The skill passed this particular case in one blind run.’”

O2.citation: “Repeat the case in fresh, context-free agents,” run additional representative and boundary cases, and “Report per-case pass rates.”

O3.citation: “the fresh runner saw only the case input, never the bar or expected outcome” and “Have an independent judge grade the artifact against the case bar.”

O4.citation: The artifact requires rerunning “the entire suite,” but does not distinguish skill defects from bad cases; instead, it says to “Map every failure to a skill defect.”

O5.citation: “Until that sweep shows sustained success,” no durable claim is supported, and the artifact requires reporting “per-case pass rates” and “before/after results.”

S1.citation: The smell is absent: the artifact explicitly says one run is “not proof.”

S2.citation: The smell is absent: it withholds a durable guidebook claim “Until that sweep shows sustained success.”

S3.citation: The smell is absent: it requires fresh repetitions and reporting “per-case pass rates.”

S4.citation: The smell is absent: “the fresh runner saw only the case input, never the bar or expected outcome.”

S5.citation: The smell is absent: it places failure mapping before edits and says to “edit only where the evidence supports it.”

rationale: The artifact correctly treats the single pass as provisional and specifies blind repetitions, runner/judge separation, per-case pass rates, full-suite reruns, and before/after evidence. It fails the required defect-versus-bad-case diagnosis because it categorically maps every failure to a skill defect rather than considering that the case or grading bar may be invalid.
